title: Reverse degreewise currying with its evaluation equation
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings in universe $\max(u,v)$, $K,L,M$ cochain complexes of $R$-module sheaves and $n\in\mathbb Z$. Using the Hom product projections and presheaf-to-sheaf tensor maps of [def-sc-hom-tensor-degreewise-equation], and $T=\operatorname{Tot}(K\otimes_R L)$ of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], there exists a morphism $b:\mathcal Hom^n(T,M)\to\mathcal Hom^n(K,\mathcal Hom(L,M))$. For every $p,q$, object $U$, section $s$ of $\mathcal Hom^n(T,M)$ over $U$, localization $W\to U$, $x\in K^p(W)$ and $y\in L^q(W)$, the $(p+q,p+q+n)$ component of $s$ evaluated on the image of $x\otimes y$ in $T^{p+q}(W)$ equals the $q$ component of the $p$ component of $b_U(s)$ evaluated first on $x$ and then on $y$ at the identity localization over $W$. No forward map and no inverse identity are assumed or asserted.

proof.text: Restrict each localized morphism from a total tensor term to M to each tensor summand K^p tensor L^q. Precompose with the presheaf-to-sheaf tensor map. This gives the balanced bilinear map (x,y) sent to s(x tensor y) on every further localization. Curry it in y and then x using the localized tensor-Hom adjunction.

Assemble the q components by the inner Hom product universal property, then the p components by the outer Hom product universal property. The component constructions are linear in s. Restriction of the bilinear evaluation map commutes with currying and the product projections, so these sectionwise maps form a sheaf-module morphism b.

Project the assembled morphism b to p and q, then evaluate at x and y at the identity localization. The product lift projection formulas recover the two curried maps; the tensor-Hom evaluation formula recovers the original balanced bilinear map. This gives the displayed evaluation equality, without either composite identity.

theorem homTensorDegreewise_reverse_construct (K L M : CochainComplex Mod ℤ) (n : ℤ) :
    letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory R
    ∃ b : (homComplex (R := R)
        (CochainComplex.mapBifunctor K L (curriedTensor Mod)) M).X n ⟶
      (homComplex (R := R) K (homComplex (R := R) L M)).X n,
      ∀ (p q : ℤ) (U : Cᵒᵖ)
    (s : (homComplex (R := R)
      (CochainComplex.mapBifunctor K L (curriedTensor Mod)) M).X n |>.val.obj U)
    (W : (Over U.unop)ᵒᵖ) (x : (K.X p).val.obj (op W.unop.left))
    (y : (L.X q).val.obj (op W.unop.left)),
    let φ := ((homTensorCurryProjection R
      (CochainComplex.mapBifunctor K L (curriedTensor Mod)) M
      n (p + q) (p + q + n) rfl).val.app U).hom s
    let ψ := ((homTensorCurryProjection R K (homComplex (R := R) L M)
      n p (p + n) rfl).val.app U).hom ((b.val.app U).hom s)
    let χ := ((homTensorCurryProjection R L M (p + n) q (p + q + n)
      (by omega)).val.app (op W.unop.left)).hom ((ψ.app W).hom x)
    (φ.app W).hom
      (((CochainComplex.ιMapBifunctor K L (curriedTensor Mod)
        p q (p + q) rfl).val.app (op W.unop.left)).hom
        (((homTensorCurrySectionMap R (K.X p) (L.X q)).app (op W.unop.left)).hom
          (x ⊗ₜ[R.obj.obj (op W.unop.left)] y))) =
      (χ.app (op (Over.mk (𝟙 W.unop.left)))).hom y
